nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Short, intense alpine summers drive plant growth, and the growing season ends early at high elevation.

nodes.name: Snowpack and glacier melt
nodes.desc: Winter snow and melting glaciers feed the streams and lakes and set the length of the growing season on the high slopes. Glaciers in the park have shrunk sharply since the 1800s.

nodes.name: Wildfire
nodes.desc: Fire is a regular part of the park and burns several thousand acres in an average year. It opens forest and clears ground for sun-loving plants.

nodes.name: Mountain soils
nodes.desc: Thin soils on rock and glacial debris supply nutrients to plants, topped up as dead matter is broken down.

nodes.name: Fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, animals and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Bunchgrasses
nodes.desc: Fescue-type grasses cover open slopes and meadows and are staple grazing for elk, sheep and goats.

nodes.name: Fireweed
nodes.desc: A tall wildflower that thrives on burned and disturbed ground. GloBI records mule deer and elk feeding on it.

nodes.name: Glacier lily
nodes.desc: Yellow lily that blooms right after snowmelt. Its corms are dug up by grizzlies and ground squirrels.

nodes.name: Saskatoon serviceberry
nodes.desc: A berry-bearing shrub of open slopes. Bears, birds and browsing ungulates use its fruit and leaves.

nodes.name: Whitebark pine
nodes.desc: High-elevation pine whose fat seeds feed nutcrackers, squirrels and bears. Blister rust has killed many trees in the park.

nodes.name: Columbian Ground Squirrel
nodes.desc: Burrowing squirrel of meadows and slopes that eats plants and bulbs. It is a prey of many predators and one of the best-recorded mammals near the park.

nodes.name: American red squirrel
nodes.desc: Forest squirrel that stores cones and seeds in middens. Bears raid middens for whitebark pine seeds.

nodes.name: Snowshoe hare
nodes.desc: Browses and grazes in forests, with a white winter coat. It is the main prey of Canada lynx.

nodes.name: Clark's nutcracker
nodes.desc: Corvid that harvests whitebark pine seeds and caches them across the slopes. Uneaten caches grow into new trees.

nodes.name: Elk
nodes.desc: Large grazer and browser of grasses, plants, leaves and bark. It is the main large prey of wolves and its carcasses feed scavengers.

nodes.name: Mountain goat
nodes.desc: The park symbol. Eats grasses, herbs, sedges, mosses and lichens high on cliffs and alpine slopes.

nodes.name: Bighorn sheep
nodes.desc: Grazes grasses and forbs on open slopes and rocky ground, moving down to winter ranges.

nodes.name: American marten
nodes.desc: Slender forest carnivore. GloBI records show it eating red squirrels and snowshoe hares.

nodes.name: Canada lynx
nodes.desc: Hare specialist; snowshoe hares make up most of its diet and lynx numbers follow the hare cycle. Listed as threatened in the US.

nodes.name: Wolverine
nodes.desc: Scavenges large mammal carcasses such as deer and elk, and also hunts ground squirrels, marmots and hares.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: Clever omnivore and scavenger that feeds at carcasses and takes small prey.

nodes.name: Grizzly bear
nodes.desc: Omnivore of lilies, berries, roots, ground squirrels, whitebark pine caches and elk. The Glacier area is a core of the northern Rockies population.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: Eliminated from the park by the 1930s and recolonized naturally from the 1980s; preys on elk and other ungulates.
